tei:titleStmt.tei:title: הוֹשַֽׁעְנוֹת לַפּוּרִים
Hosha'not for Purim, by Avraham Menaḥem Mendel Mohr (1855)

tei:div.tei:head: Hosha'not for Purim, by Avraham Menaḥem Mendel Mohr (1855)

tei:lg.tei:l: Please save us, for your sake, our wine, please save us!
Please save us, for your sake, our juice, please save us!
Please save us, for your sake, our vine, please save us!
Please save us, for your sake, our mead, please save us!

Please save us, for the sake of your truth... your vineworker... your goblet... your fish... your hin-measure... your meetings...your grapeskins... your grapeseeds... your tastes... your presses... your vineyards... your pancakes... your delicacies... your songs... your grapebuds... your grapes... your law-interpreters... your raisins... your plates... your many friends... your drink... your juice, please save us!

Please save us, drinking stein... squeezed winepress... salted fish... righteous hin... and laughter will be seen... glutton and gorger... barrel of mead... slaughtering for meat... burnt wine... full cup... hazelnut and walnut... oven maker... lentil soup... fleshpot... flowing chestnut... mouth-openers... fire-roasted... abomasum and stomach... pressed headcheese... inebriates of Ephraim... juice and oil, please save us!
Have mercy, please, on the community of the inebriates;
send and fill their throats,
and give drink to us, o wine, our drink!
Open the gates of the cellar,
and open your good wine for us;
tilt us and don’t pour water,
and give drink to us, o cocktail, our burnt-wine!

tei:l.tei:note: The voice of the intoxicator intoxicates and says!

tei:lg.tei:l: Counted and finished, in the counsel of the drink-sages,
better for a man to drink than not to drink!
Celebrate and rejoice in the joy of Purim,
and give honor to the community of inebriates,
for wine is good for the poor and the rich!
More than gold or priceless pearls,
let us cheer and celebrate in the press and vinery,
for they are for us strength and light!
I will praise my wine and rejoice in it,
that I may place my drinking in it.
I will give a sip in the counsel of the close people;
my wine and juice I will be quenched with!
Let us cheer...
In each mouth I will empty your goblet,
and with a bold neck I will drink your vessel;
in celebration you will guide us to your house’
for your strength and for your taste!
Let us cheer...
Vine, hasten good beverage,
for you are strong and good inebriation.
Your mighty men will drink you with a good mouth.
Praise wine for it is good!
Let us cheer...
Mead, give my myriads drink please,
for none is like you in my eyes.
Fish will surround you before me.
Who can tell the achievements of my delicacies?
Let us cheer...
It it not so? In love, it chose us —
the blood of grapes — gave us drink.
The red red stuff intoxicated us,
for forever is its kindness with us!
Let us cheer...

tei:note.tei:p: A pun on the name of Haman’s son Parshandata as parshan (interpreter) data (the law). Rashi hinself is referred to as ”a parshandata” in some texts of the time.
A pun on the Foundation Stone, which is homophonous in Hebrew.
A measurement of wine, around six litres (1.6 gallons).
A pun on Isaac and mount Moriah.

Note: the Hebrew says dvash, “honey.” This might refer to sweet wine, wine with honey added, or some other fermented honey product. I’ve chosen to consistently translate it as “mead” to preserve the implications of ”honey” and ”alcoholic.”
